source_text: Τοῦτο δὴ τοῦθ᾽ οὕτως ἔχειν νομίσας, ἔγνων ἐπὶ ἑτέραν ἰδέαν τραπέσθαι βίου, καὶ ἐκδοῦναι μὲν ἐμαυτὸν τρυφῇ, πεῖραν δὲ λαβεῖν ἡδονῶν ποικίλων. Νῦν τοίνυν συνῆκα ὡς τὰ τοιαῦτα μάταια σύμπαντα· καὶ γέλωτα μὲν εἰκῆ φερόμενον ἐπέσχον, ἡδονὴν δὲ πρὸς τὸ σωφρονεῖν ἐκόλασα, πικρῶς ἐπιτιμήσας αὐτῇ. Λογισάμενος δέ, ὅτι ψυχὴ δύναται στῆσαι μεθύουσαν καὶ ῥέουσαν ὥσπερ οἶνον σώματος φύσιν, ἐγκράτεια δὲ δουλοῦται ἐπιθυμίαν· προεθυμήθην κατιδεῖν, τί ποτε εἴη προκείμενον ἀνθρώποις σπουδαῖον, καὶ τῷ ὄντι καλὸν ὃ καταπράξονται παρὰ τουτονὶ τὸν βίον. Διεξελήλυθα γὰρ τὰ λοιπὰ σύμπαντα ὅσ᾽ ἀξιάγαστα νομίζεται, οἴκων τε ὑπερυψήλων ἀνορθώσεις καὶ φυτείας ἀμπέλων, ἔτι δὲ παραδείσων κατασκευάς, καὶ παντοίων δένδρων καρποφόρων κτήσεις καὶ ἐπιμελείας· ὅπου δὲ καὶ δεξαμεναὶ μεγάλαι πρὸς ὑποδοχὰς ὑδάτων κατεσκευάσθησαν, εἰς δαψιλῆ ἀρδείαν τῶν φυτῶν ἀπονενεμημέναι. Περιεβαλόμην δὲ καὶ οἰκετῶν πλῆθος, θεράποντας καὶ θεραπαίνας· ἄλλους μὲν ἔξωθεν κτησάμενος, ἄλλους δὲ καὶ παρ᾽ ἐμαυτῷ γενομένους καρπωσάμενος. Ζώων δὲ τετραπόδων ἀγέλαι, πολλαὶ μὲν βουκολίων, πολλαὶ δὲ ποιμνίων ὑπὸ τὴν ἐμὴν ἦλθον ἐξουσίαν παρ᾽ ὁντινοῦν τῶν πάλαι. Θησαυροί τε χρυσοῦ τε καὶ ἀργύρου προσέρρεον, δορυφόρους τέ μοι καὶ δασμοφόρους, τοὺς ἁπάντων βασιλεῖς πεποιημένῳ. Χοροί τε συνεκροτοῦντο παμπληθεῖς, ἀρρένων δέ τε ὁμοῦ καὶ θηλειῶν εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν τέρψιν, παναρμόνιον ἐκπονούντων ᾠδήν. Συμπόσιά γε μὴν καὶ οἰνοχόους εἰς τοῦτο ἀπέταξα τῆς τρυφῆς μέρος ἐξ ἑκατέρου γένους ἀνθρώπων ἐξειλεγμένους, οὐδ᾽ ἂν καταλέγειν ἔχοιμι, τοσοῦτον ὑπερέβαλον τούτοις τοὺς πρὸ ἐμοῦ βασιλεύσαντας Ἱερουσαλήμ. Εἶτα συνέβαινε, τὰ μὲν τῆς σοφίας μοι ἐλαττοῦσθαι, πληθύνειν δὲ τὰ τῆς οὐκ ἀγαθῆς ἐπιθυμίας. Παντὶ γὰρ ὀφθαλμῶν τε δελεάσματι, καὶ καρδίας ἀκράτοις ὁρμαῖς ἐφιεὶς πανταχόθεν προσπιπτούσαις, ἡδονῶν ἐλπίσιν ἐμαυτὸν ἐκδεδωκώς· καὶ πάσαις τρυφαῖς δειλαίαις, τὴν ἐμαυτοῦ ἐγκατέδησα προαίρεσιν. Οὕτω γάρ μου αἱ ἐνθυμήσεις, εἰς δυσπραγίαν ἠνέχθησαν, ὡς ταῦτα μὲν εἶναι καλά, ταῦτα δέ μοι προσήκειν διαπράττεσθαι νομίζειν. Εἶτα ποτὲ ἀνανήψας ἐγὼ καὶ ἀναβλέψας, κατεῖδον ἅπερ ἐν χερσὶν εἶχον, μοχθηρὰ ὁμοῦ καὶ παγχάλεπα, πνεύματος οὐκ ἀγαθοῦ ποιήματα. Οὐδὲν γὰρ ὁτιοῦν ὑπ᾽ ἀνθρώπων ᾑρημένον, ἀποδεκτὸν εἶναί μοι νῦν καταφαίνεται καὶ περισπούδαστον ὀρθῷ λογισμῷ.
thought_title: Testing pleasure and great works and finding them futile
orientation: Solomon, as reported by Gregory, turns from searching wisdom to testing a life of luxury, pleasure and great building works.
pass_a_gloss: Having supposed that this very thing holds thus, I decided to turn to another form of life, and to give myself over to luxury, and to take trial of varied pleasures. Now therefore I understood that such things are all futile altogether; and laughter being carried along at random I held back, and pleasure I chastised toward being self-controlled, having rebuked it bitterly. And having reckoned that a soul is able to make stand firm a nature of the body that is drunken and flowing like wine, and that self-control enslaves desire, I became eager beforehand to look down to see what earnest pursuit might ever be lying before men, and what in reality is good which they will accomplish during this life. For I went through all the remaining things as many as are deemed worthy of wonder, both erections of exceedingly high houses and plantings of vineyards, and further constructions of parks, and acquisitions and carings of all kinds of fruit-bearing trees; where also great reservoirs for receptions of waters were constructed, allotted for abundant watering of the plants. And I surrounded myself with a multitude of household servants, male servants and female servants; some I acquired from outside, and others born beside myself I gained. And herds of four-footed animals, many of cattle and many of flocks, came under my authority beyond anyone of old. And treasures both of gold and of silver flowed in, with spearmen and tribute-bearers to me, with me having made the kings of all. And very numerous choruses were assembled together, of males and females for my delight, working out a fully harmonious song. And banquets and cupbearers, chosen from each kind of men, I appointed for this part of luxury, which I could not even enumerate, so much did I surpass in these things those who had been kings before me in Jerusalem. Then it happened that the things of wisdom were diminished for me, and the things of the not good desire were multiplied. For yielding to every bait of the eyes and to unmixed impulses of the heart falling upon me from everywhere, having given myself over to hopes of pleasures, and to all wretched luxuries, I bound down my own resolve. For thus my thoughts were carried up into ill-doing, so as to suppose that these things are good, and that it befits me to accomplish these things. Then at some time having become sober and having looked up, I looked down upon what things I had in my hands, toilsome together and very grievous, works of a not good spirit. For nothing whatever chosen by men appears to me now acceptable and much pursued by right reckoning.

pass_b_english: Solomon continues: Convinced that things stood just so, I decided to turn to a different way of life. I would give myself to luxury and try pleasures of every kind. Now I see that all such things are futile altogether. I held back laughter when it ran loose, and I disciplined pleasure toward being self-controlled, rebuking it bitterly. I had reasoned that the soul can steady a bodily nature that gets drunk and flows like wine, and that self-control enslaves desire. So I became eager to see what earnest pursuit lies before people, and what truly good thing they will accomplish in this life.

I went through all the rest of the things people count admirable. I raised towering houses and planted vineyards, and I laid out gardens and acquired fruit trees of every kind and tended them (Ecclesiastes 2:4-6). There also I had great reservoirs built to hold water, set apart to water the plants abundantly. I surrounded myself with a crowd of household servants, menservants and maidservants, some bought from abroad and others born in my own house and raised there. Herds of four-footed animals came under my power, many cattle and many flocks, beyond anyone from earlier times. Treasures of gold and silver poured in to me, since I had made the kings of all nations my guards and tribute-bearers. Vast choirs were gathered for my delight, men and women together, performing a song in full harmony. For this side of luxury I appointed feasts and cupbearers, chosen from people of either sex, too many for me even to count; in these things I far surpassed those who had reigned in Jerusalem before me.

Then it came about that wisdom lessened in me, while desire for what was not good grew. I yielded to every lure of the eyes and to the unrestrained impulses of the heart that assailed me from all sides, and I gave myself over to hopes of pleasures. I bound my own choice to all those wretched luxuries. My thoughts were thus carried into misery, so that I judged these things good and judged that I ought to do them.

Then at last I came to myself and looked up. I saw that the things in my hands were troublesome and altogether hard, works of a spirit that was not good. For nothing chosen by people now appears to me acceptable and worth pursuing when judged by right reason.
notes: clause with δορυφόρους καὶ δασμοφόρους, τοὺς ἁπάντων βασιλεῖς πεποιημένῳ is syntactically compressed; glossed as it stands without supplying missing words

problems.quote: with guards and tribute-bearers, since I had been made king over all.
problems.source_quote: δορυφόρους τέ μοι καὶ δασμοφόρους, τοὺς ἁπάντων βασιλεῖς πεποιημένῳ
problems.why: The Greek says Solomon made the kings of all nations his guards and tribute-bearers. The English instead says he was made king over all, which reverses agency and drops the kings as subjects.
problems.fix: Treasures of gold and silver poured in to me, since I had made the kings of all nations my guards and tribute-bearers.

edits.old: with guards and tribute-bearers, since I had been made king over all.
edits.new: since I had made the kings of all nations my guards and tribute-bearers.

fixed: Fixed agency reversal: source τοὺς ἁπάντων βασιλεῖς πεποιημένῳ has Solomon making the kings his δορυφόρους and δασμοφόρους, not being made king himself.

last_rejected.quote: some bought from abroad and others born in my own house and raised there
last_rejected.source_quote: ἄλλους μὲν ἔξωθεν κτησάμενος, ἄλλους δὲ καὶ παρ᾽ ἐμαυτῷ γενομένους καρπωσάμενος
last_rejected.why: ἔξωθεν κτησάμενος is acquired from outside, not bought abroad; καρπωσάμενος means he reaped them as gain, not that he raised them.
last_rejected.fix: some I acquired from outside, and others, born in my own house, I took as my profit.
last_rejected.ruling: ἔξωθεν κτησάμενος = acquired from outside; 'bought from abroad' is a slight narrowing but within sense. καρπωσάμενος 'raised' is loose yet not meaning-changing; παρ᾽ ἐμαυτῷ γενομένους = born in my house.
